## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This adds a dedicated `sensor` entity for Sonos favorites which is disabled by default. The state of the sensor displays the number of favorites. The "items" attribute is a dictionary which is keyed by the `media_content_id` and includes the item name as the value.

Example template use-cases:
```
# Get all favorite names as a list (old behavior)
{{ state_attr("sensor.sonos_favorites", "items").values() | list }}

# Pick a specific favorite name by position
{{ (state_attr("sensor.sonos_favorites", "items").values() | list)[3] }}

# Pick a random item's `media_content_id`
{{ state_attr("sensor.sonos_favorites", "items") | list | random }}

# Loop through and grab name & media_content_id
{% for media_id, name in state_attr("sensor.sonos_favorites", "items").items() %}
  {{ name, media_id }}
{% endfor %}
```

This is an alternative approach to address the breaking change from 2022.4.0 (#67931).

Fixes #69788
Fixes #70021

issue_context.title: Attribute source_list does not exist any more
issue_context.body:
### The problem

According to the  discussion [How to access the media source list in templates? ](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/how-to-access-the-media-source-list-in-templates/409903) the `source_list` attribute was intentionally removed in version 2022.4.1.

This breaks templates accessing this attribute.

Is there a (currently undocumented) way to access the favorites list of sonos in templates?


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.4.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.3.7

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

Sonos

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sonos/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
{{state_attr('media_player.myradio', 'source_list') }}
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @cgtobi, @jjlawren, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`sonos`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L951) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Can I ask what specific use-cases you had for the `source list` + templates? The attribute held an an (effectively) unordered list of strings. Perhaps there is an alternative approach.
I need to access the whole list, e.g. for text2speech purposes to tell, what choice you have.

> Can I ask what specific use-cases you had for the `source list` + templates? The attribute held an an (effectively) unordered list of strings. Perhaps there is an alternative approach.

I implemented an alarm clock, which plays a user-selected favourite on a Sonos box. The favourite is selectable in the UI (input select). A Python script fills the input select based on the source_list-attribute. 
As the attribute is missing now, the script no longer works. As a workaround I hardcoded the favourite list.

@tdejneka the `capabilities.source_list` in the entity registry is created by core and not actively maintained by the integration so it's not dynamic. I believe it's just a snapshot of what the `source_list` looked like when the speaker was created. It unfortunately can't be relied upon for this.

Thanks for the explanation; I wasn't aware of that. 

When using the Media Browser to browse a Sonos speaker, where is it sourcing the content for Favorites > Radio?

The favorites are just broken down into categories, just like in the native Sonos app. Instead of one long list of names (the old `source_list` way), it separates out tracks, albums, radio, playlists, etc.

Understood but where are the media content names stored?

For example, I have a Sonos Favorite called Concert Hall (visible in the Sonos app). In Home Assistant, it appears in Media Browser > Favorites > Radio > Concert Hall. Where is Home Assistant's Media Browser getting this information from?

When I use VS Code to search all of Home Assistant's files (in all sub-directories), the only place the string Concert Hall is found is in `core.entity_registry` (once for each Sonos speaker). However, you said that location isn't dynamically maintained by the Sonos integration and only represents a snapshot when the media_player entity was created. So if not from there, where is Media Browser getting its dynamic information from?

Is it polling the Sonos integration to dynamically acquire the latest Favorites directly from the speaker?
The frontend makes a websocket API call. Nothing is intentionally stored to the state machine or filesystem anymore.

Thanks again; I appreciate the insight.

OK so the Websocket API call queries the Sonos speaker to get the latest list of Favorites? I assume it makes a call to the Sonos integration to get it? 

Would you happen to know the details of the Websocket API call? I browsed the documentation but failed to find something describing how to query media content.
The websocket API is only used by the frontend today. There is currently no supported way to query it using templates or automations.

That's good to know but the question remains how does the Websocket API call get the latest list of Favorites?  Given that the information isn't stored anywhere by Home Assistant, it implies the API call must query the Sonos integration to get the latest list of Favorites from the target speaker. Is that approximately what's happening?

Just trying to understand the underlying mechanism.
The available favorites are cached in memory by the integration.
Good news the Source list might return, the 'mini media player' can pull this list down to manually to access favourites instantly. At the moment it doesn't work.

review_comments: Should these be excluded from the recorder?
Yes. I guess in that case it needs to become a `sonos.favorites` entity or we need to add support for recorder platform to allow integrations to add filters for specific entities.
Hmm they don't change often as it's limited to 72 entries (lol Sonos). I am not sure if this warrants enough reason to migrate from `sensor` domain to `sonos`.
Actually it's 70 😆 and the state should only update if the user modifies the favorites from the Sonos app. I assumed that creating it as disabled by default would limit the impact.

If we rename `items` to `favorites` and add the recorder platform to this integration to exclude that attribute from recording, it would be solved?

Alternatively, change this to be an `select` instead; That way it becomes a functional thing (as people can use it to select a favorite), option can be retrieved in templating AND the options lists of a `select` is excluded from being recorded.

I started with a `select` entity, but changed my mind for a couple reasons:
1. It would require an entity per device instead of one per system and an update to favorites would write to X entities instead of one. However, it sounds like the options list isn't included in the recorder and this may be a non-issue.
2. What should a `select` entity state show if none of the available options are in use?

> What should a select entity state show if none of the available options are in use?

None?

I feel like a select would become a shitty version of the actual media player which offers favorites via the media browser. The goal of this entity is just to provide people this data for their templating.
